[FOSSIL](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.09152) adds a history-similarity vector to a weighted recent-item sum, sharing item factors across branches. Long-term pooling scales by |history excluding candidate|^−α; experiments fix α=0.2. Recent lag k receives a learned global coefficient plus user-specific offset, ηk+ηuk. These are unconstrained lag weights, without softmax normalization, monotonic decay, or elapsed-time dependence. Fusion is additive; no sigmoid mixture gate or explicit branch L2 normalization. Comparisons examine component contributions and Markov order, rather than learned gates versus matched fixed fusion.

[LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/html/2407.14743v1) averages Transformer outputs within sessions, models historical session evolution with a GRU, and uses candidate-conditioned softmax attention pooling. Short-term modeling combines current-session pooling with optional Time4LSTM encoding of recent items. Fusion uses α=sigmoid(W[long;short;candidate]+b), followed by α·long+(1−α)·short and an MLP scorer. The fusion equations specify no explicit branch norm matching; recency comes from session thresholds, recent-window selection, and Time4LSTM, rather than one exponential-decay parameter. Reported ablations remove encoders, denoising, or recent-interest components; they do not isolate the gate against matched fixed mixtures. [HGN](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1906.09217) instead gates features and instances before pooling, then adds long-term, pooled short-term, and item-pair scores.

Suggested SASRec controls: baseline; fixed recent-history residual; learned global mixture; contextual sigmoid gate. Match branch normalization, window, and parameter budget; compare uniform pooling with normalized exponential weights exp(−λ·lag), separating event lag from elapsed time. Measure branch norms and gate saturation. Durable-purchase over-specialization is a hypothesis, not established by these papers; inspect validation performance across categories and time gaps without inventing purchase-intent labels.
